title: Introduce tenant snooze horizon + proactive egress hedge to smooth SLO violations during transient regional pressure
author: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Context: We observed recurring short-lived regional pressure spikes that caused many tenants to cross soft SLOs while the system rebalanced. Two failure modes made the surface impact worse: 1) immediate per-tenant circuit tripping created churn (rapid open/close cycles) that amplified downstream KV-cache drains; 2) proactive egress fallbacks were too aggressive and flooded neighboring regions during bursts, causing cascading latency spikes. Motivation: Reduce customer-visible SLO violations from transient events by (a) allowing a short 'snooze horizon' where a tenant's SLO state is softly paused to let in-flight work and KV caches settle, and (b) adding a conservative egress "hedge" that rate-limits cross-region fallback traffic during ramp windows. This change is intended as a safe, backward-compatible reliability smoothing mechanism with explicit telemetry and an escape hatch.

What this PR does (high level): 1) Adds TenantSnoozeHorizon: a temporal pauser that, when a tenant's short-term error/latency rate breaches a configured soft threshold, will: - mark the tenant as "snoozed" for a configurable horizon (default 18s) - avoid flipping the tenant's circuit to hard-open during the horizon - allow evictions/drains to continue but reduce aggressive eviction triggers - surface a per-tenant telemetry tag (snooze_state=entered/exited) for post-mortem analysis 2) Implements EgressHedge: a cross-region egress-rate limiter that: - applies a token-bucket hedge on fallbacks routed out-of-region during a tenant snooze or cluster ramp event - uses conservative defaults plus a per-tenant weight to avoid blanket throttles - exposes metrics for dropped/hedged requests so we can tune safely 3) Grandfathering logic: tenants under active canary or pinned model versions are exempted by default; config flag available for opt-in. 4) Adds a KV-drain escort hook: in the rare case of node evacuation, we detect in-flight KV cache syncs and extend the snooze horizon by a short delta to avoid cold-KV-induced retries that would otherwise spike errors.

Changeset summary (commits): - c1a2b3e: introduce TenantSnoozeHorizon state machine, unit tests, and basic telemetry - d4f5g6h: add EgressHedge token-bucket implementation and integration tests - e7h8i9j: KV-drain escort hook + small refactor to request routing to add a fast-path flag - k0l1m2n: config knobs and runtime feature flag (snooze.horizon_seconds, egress.hedge_rate) - p3q4r5s: docs and release notes + changelog entry

Files changed (high level): ["serving/core/snooze_horizon.go", "serving/core/snooze_horizon_test.go", "serving/egress/hedge_limiter.go", "serving/egress/hedge_limiter_test.go", "serving/kv/escort.go", "config/defaults.yaml", "docs/operational/snooze_and_egress_hedge.md"].

Testing and validation: - Unit tests cover state machine transitions, token-bucket boundaries, and eviction exceptions. - Integration test harness simulated regional spike (ramp 0->500 rps over 6s) with and without the snooze+hedge enabled; result: 62% reduction in transient SLO breaches and 41% fewer cross-region fallback spikes in the simulated topology. - CI: full unit/integration suite passed; one flaky egress integration test failed on first run (timer race), rerun succeeded. - Staging rollout: live staging cluster ran the feature behind runtime flag for 48 hours under synthetic traffic; no regressions seen in cost or long-tail p95.

Review conversation (high level): - Asha: requested clearer docs around opt-outs for pinned tenants and a default horizon rationale. Response: added docs and a new config comment explaining 18s empiric basis (observed median settle time + safety margin). - Miguel: asked about interaction with autoscaler and if snoozing could delay scale-up. Response: clarified autoscaler still uses raw demand signals; snooze only affects circuit decisions and eviction aggressiveness, does not block node scale-up. Added integration assertion to prove separation. - Liang: suggested exposing per-tenant hedged_drops metric; implemented and wired to tracing. - Dana: asked for rollback plan; added runtime feature flag and a kill-switch endpoint and documented steps.

Rollout plan and risk mitigation: - Feature behind runtime flag default: off for Hosted, on for Dedicated and Private by opt-in. - Canary rollout: 1% of tenants for first 24h, then 10% if no regressions, 100% after a week. - Monitoring: new dashboards (snooze.entered, snooze.exited, egress.hedged, egress.dropped) and an alert if hedged_drops > 0.5% of baseline traffic for 5m. - Rollback: turn off runtime flag or set hedge_rate to high value; documented rollback steps.

Release notes: - Stabilizes short-lived SLO blips during regional pressure by introducing Tenant Snooze Horizon and Proactive Egress Hedge. Enabled behind runtime feature flag. See docs/operational/snooze_and_egress_hedge.md for configuration and tuning guidance.

Why this is different: rather than hard circuit flipping or immediate tenant quarantine we introduce a time-based soft window (snooze) and a conservative egress throttle that cooperate to let the system settle without penalizing tenants with rapid churn. The approach aims to reduce cascade effects from KV-coldness and cross-region floodback while preserving safety and observability.
review_comments: Asha Patel: Please explain why 18s default - what data backs this?
Sofia Nguyen: Added explanation in docs; 18s = median settle(9s) * 2 buffer + 0.5s housekeeping. Also added runtime knob.
Miguel Torres: Will snoozing slow down autoscaler?
Sofia Nguyen: No - autoscaler uses raw metrics; snooze only affects eviction and circuit decisions. Added integration assertion.
Liang Wu: Add per-tenant hedged_drops metric so we can tune.
Sofia Nguyen: Implemented hedged_drops and added to tracing tags.
Dana Rivera: Need rollback plan and kill-switch.
Sofia Nguyen: Added runtime flag and kill-switch docs + steps.
Asha Patel: Approve after docs update.
